overview: The two sequential steps of gene expression: copying DNA into RNA, then reading that RNA to build a protein.
genZNote: Transcription copies the note. Translation reads it out loud in a different language.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Synthesis of an RNA copy (typically mRNA) from a DNA template.
aspects.valueB: Synthesis of a polypeptide chain by reading an mRNA sequence via the ribosome.

aspects.label: Target Molecule
aspects.valueA: DNA template strand is read to produce RNA.
aspects.valueB: mRNA is read (as codons) to produce protein.

aspects.label: Cellular Location
aspects.valueA: Nucleus in eukaryotes; cytoplasm in prokaryotes.
aspects.valueB: Cytoplasm, at ribosomes (free or ER-bound) in both eukaryotes and prokaryotes.

aspects.label: Mechanism
aspects.valueA: RNA polymerase binds a promoter and synthesizes RNA 5' to 3', complementary to the template strand.
aspects.valueB: Ribosome moves along mRNA codon by codon; tRNAs deliver matching amino acids via anticodon pairing.

aspects.label: Products
aspects.valueA: Pre-mRNA (eukaryotes, further processed by splicing/capping/polyadenylation) or mature mRNA (prokaryotes).
aspects.valueB: A polypeptide chain, which folds and may be further modified into a functional protein.

aspects.label: Key Molecules Involved
aspects.valueA: RNA polymerase, promoter sequences, transcription factors.
aspects.valueB: Ribosomes (rRNA + proteins), tRNA, mRNA, start/stop codons.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: DNA to RNA, occurs first, happens in the nucleus (eukaryotes).
aspects.valueB: RNA to protein, occurs second, happens in the cytoplasm.

overlay.memoryTrick: "Transcription: DNA to RNA, same language (nucleic acid). Translation: RNA to protein, new language (amino acids)."
